text:
ops-bot: ALERT: egress bandwidth saturation detected in eu-west-2 on rack-r3 (NIC 400Gbps). Affected pools: tenant-shared-3, reserved-acme. Auto-fallback to backup-egress-route triggered at 15:02:18 UTC.

alex: noticed a downstream latency spike ~15:00, thanks for the alert. are we seeing packet drops or just pacing?

maria: tcp retransmits up ~18% on nodes 3/4 in rack-r3, qdisc counters show bursts around tenant-acme flows.

jin: tenant-acme has been pushing big embedding exports — likely saturating egress and stealing NIC queue. That explains noisy neighbor.

alex: current fallback routed traffic to spare-egress-az-b. Does that create cross-az cost concerns?

taylor: yes, spare-egress-az-b incurs inter-az egress and a small latency hit. Cost hit estimated ~ $0.02/hr for affected flows but depends on sustained bytes.

sam: short-term mitigation idea: reduce tenant-acme burst-window from 10s -> 2s via shaping on their soft-quota. Could we do a soft-throttle instead of immediate pool handoff?

maria: we already have soft-shaping rules but tenant-acme is above soft threshold. Their requests are short but extremely bursty (many small requests). shaping helps but NIC queue refill is faster.

jin: config snippet I ran locally to reproduce shaping:
```
qdisc add dev eth0 root fq_codel limit 1000
tc filter add dev eth0 protocol ip parent 1:0 u32 match ip dst 0.0.0.0/0 flowid 1:1
```
not production, but shows head-of-line behavior.

alex: long term we need a handoff that preserves intra-az routing when possible. Proposal: a two-stage fallback — first apply per-tenant pacing at edge proxy for 30s, then if sustained, promote to cross-az fallback.

taylor: sounds reasonable. we should parameterize: pacing-ms, window-sec, promotion-threshold-bps. Also calc expected cost delta when promoting.

sam: can we do predictive preemption instead? if tenant-acme usage correlates with hourly cron, we could pre-warm dedicated pool for their peak window. Saves cost vs cross-az fallback.

maria: they do nightly bulk exports 03:00-04:00 UTC, but this spike is during business hours. looks ad-hoc.

jin: another angle: enable NIC-level tenant isolation for reserved pools (SR-iso). That would cap egress per-tenant at hardware queue. Requires firmware flags and ~2hr deploy. Not ideal for immediate.

ops-bot: NOTE: fallback routing completed. 18 flows still on original egress, 102 flows moved.

alex: immediate action list: 1) apply temporary pacing at edge proxy for tenant-acme (sam), 2) monitor retransmits and queue depth (maria), 3) calculate cross-az egress cost if escalation required (taylor), 4) run quick audit of tenant export cron schedules (jin).

sam: starting proxy pacing now: `proxyctl set-rate tenant-acme 5mbps --burst 256kb --window 2s`

maria: seeing queue depth fall after ~40s. retransmits down to +6% (was 18%). good sign.

taylor: cost calc: if we had promoted all flows to az-b for 30m, estimated additional egress ~1.8TB -> ~$0.36. not huge but repeated events add up.

jin: for postmortem: can we add metric for "fallback-promotions-per-tenant" and alert when single tenant triggers >3 promotions/week?

alex: yes, and add a runbook step to prefer pacing vs cross-az promotion unless throughput > X bps for >Y min. We'll draft thresholds.

ops-bot: INFO: incident closed for now. reopen if egress > 85% on any rack for 10m. :white_check_mark:

sam: follow-up PR for proxy pacing defaults incoming. will include a safe rollback.

maria: I'll draft alert tuning and the new dashboard panel for queue depth + retransmits.

alex: thanks team. postmortem item: investigate NIC queue sizing and whether per-tenant HW isolation is feasible without firmware upgrades.

jin: leaving notes in #eng-infra-docs about the two-stage fallback proposal.

sam: ping me if you need the `proxyctl` wrapper script.

alex: nice triage, closing thread. :thumbsup:
